scope: Audit the 1963 successor teacher-duty regime using an official Ministry of Government Legislation interpretation that reconstructs the original Private School Act Article 55 lineage, and pin the repeal rationale/text of Law No.708.

findings.claim: Private School Act Article 55 dates unchanged from the original 1963 enactment and was designed to bridge private-school teacher service duties to the public-teacher service regime.
findings.evidence: MOLEG interpretation 11-0492 (2011-10-27) expressly states Article 55 has remained unchanged since enactment by Law No.1362 on 1963-06-26 and reconstructs its original legal function through former Education Public Officials Act Article 43.

findings.claim: Former Education Public Officials Act Article 43 supplied the exact public-service bridge relevant to teacher collective activity.
findings.evidence: MOLEG 11-0492 states former Education Public Officials Act Article 43 applied State Public Officials Act Articles 53 through 67 mutatis mutandis to education public officials. That range includes Article 66 collective-action prohibition. This materially narrows the open cross-reference question left in pass 151.
findings.caution: Still obtain the 1963/1964 promulgated Education Public Officials Act text as the primary transcription target.

findings.claim: Private-school teachers were connected to Article 66 through a two-step legal bridge rather than by being declared public officials.
findings.evidence: Private School Act Art.55 -> rules concerning national/public-school teacher service -> former Education Public Officials Act Art.43 -> State Public Officials Act Arts.53-67. MOLEG also stresses that mutatis-mutandis incorporation is limited to the specified service rules and should not be expanded to unrelated public-official restrictions.

findings.claim: The collective-class-refusal dismissal mechanism for private-school teachers is distinct from the Article 55/Article 43/Article 66 service-rule bridge.
findings.evidence: MOLEG 11-0492 separately identifies Private School Act Article 58(1)(4) as a dismissal ground for political movement, collective refusal of classes, or directing/agitating students for or against a political party. It must not be collapsed into the general Article 66 prohibition or treated as the same enforcement mechanism.

findings.claim: Law No.708 was formally repealed because the government asserted that educational order had largely normalized and the temporary law no longer had practical need.
findings.evidence: The National Law Information Center repeal reason for Law No.1466 says the temporary special law had been enacted to restore disordered educational administration after May 16 and that special measures had largely restored normal order, removing practical need for continued existence.
findings.caution: This is the legislature/government's stated repeal rationale, not an independently verified sociological finding that educational order was in fact normalized.

findings.claim: Law No.1466 explicitly repealed Law No.708 with effect from 1964-01-01.
findings.evidence: The official amendment text states that Law No.708, Education Temporary Special Measures Act, is repealed; the supplementary provision makes the repeal effective 1964-01-01.

findings.claim: The 1963 permanent successor regime proves textual descent from the missing 1961-06-21 Teachers Organization Bill or Law No.708 Article 13.
findings.evidence: The service bridge is now legally verified, but no drafting-file or clause-level textual genealogy has yet been obtained. Functional continuity must remain separate from textual descent.

events.legal_authority: Education Public Officials Act former Art.43 -> State Public Officials Act Arts.53-67

events.note: Useful for statutory lineage and scope; not evidence of 1961 subjective legislative intent.

adversarial_checks: A later official interpretation can verify statutory lineage and scope but cannot by itself prove the subjective intent of 1961 drafters.
Article 55 incorporation is limited to service rules; it does not transform private teachers into public officials.
Article 58 dismissal and Article 66 collective-action prohibition are separate legal mechanisms.
The government's 1963 claim that educational order had normalized is a stated repeal rationale, not an independently established fact.
Repeal of Law 708 does not imply disappearance of overlapping permanent restrictions already embedded in the successor regime.
Functional continuity does not prove word-for-word copying.
The exact promulgated 1963 Education Public Officials Act Article 43 remains worth pinning despite the official later reconstruction.
The missing June 1961 Teachers Organization Bill remains an ancestor candidate only.
Do not infer ministerial personal authorship from institutional proposal chains.
Do not back-project later constitutional or administrative interpretations into the political motives of 1961 actors.
